Think you can't automate anything because you're not a techie? You don't need to be. You just need to ask better questions.
Let's set up a small automation that drafts, or even sends, your emails every day. No code.
Meet Goopta jee. He runs a hardware shop, and he always forgets follow-ups. Client replies, payment reminders, supplier mails.
And meet Meera, his accountant. Every month, she emails invoices and reconciliations to twelve clients, one by one.
Here's what you need. A paid Claude plan, the Claude desktop app, and your Gmail.
Step one. Open Claude's settings, go to Connectors, and connect Gmail. If you keep files in Google Drive, connect Drive too.
Step two. In the Claude app, open Scheduled from the sidebar. Tap New task, then Create with Claude.
Step three. This is where better questions matter. A vague request gets a vague result.
Don't just say, remind me about emails. Say who, what, when, and how.
Who. The exact email addresses. What. Follow up, reply, or send an update. When. Every weekday at nine. How. Short and polite, and wait for my approval.
Here's Goopta jee's request, written just like that.
Claude may ask a question or two, then shows you the task. You approve it, and it's scheduled.
Step four. Decide how much Claude can do on its own.
In the Gmail connector's settings, set sending to needs approval. Claude drafts, you review, and you hit send.
Or set it to always allow, and Claude sends on its own. On team plans, your admin may need to allow this.
Our tip. Start with approval. Go automatic only for mails that are the same every time, like a weekly reminder.
Now, Meera's version. She keeps each client's invoice and reconciliation in a Drive folder, named after the client.
Her task. On the fifth of every month, find the latest files in each client's folder, and email the Drive links to that client, with a short note.
One thing to know. The Gmail connector shares Drive links, it doesn't attach files. So check the folder's sharing first.
Now twelve client emails go out on time, every month, even when Meera is busy closing the books.
To be fair, watch the first few runs closely. And never automate a mail you wouldn't want sent by mistake.
Ten minutes of setup. Every follow-up, on time.
